description: Sync every user, group and application in your Okta org, plus System Log events. Okta permissions are not carried over.
opening: Sync every user, group and application in your Okta org, plus System Log events. Each user, group, application and log event is one document. A group lists its members, an application its assigned users, and a user the active MFA factors HydraDB found.

Okta permissions are not imported, so every synced item is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. These records do not prove who has access today or that MFA is off: a missing factor can mean a factor read failed. Users, groups and applications deleted in Okta can stay in HydraDB.

notes: Okta reads are governed by the admin role on the token, not by anything on a user, group, application or event, so there is nothing per item to import.
Application assignments and self-service settings are not treated as read permissions.

connect.auth: Okta uses an API token. The token gets the admin role of the person who creates it, so create it while signed in as a Read-only Administrator.

credentials.name: api_key
credentials.text: An Okta API token, from Security, API, Tokens, Create Token.

credentials.name: service_url
credentials.text: Your org's API address with the `/api/v1/` path and the trailing slash: `https://<org>.okta.com/api/v1/`.

connect.credentials_note: The token stops working if the account that created it is deactivated, and Okta expires a token after 30 days without use.
connect.permissions_label: What the token's admin role needs

permissions.name: Read-only Administrator
permissions.text: the role of the person who creates the token.

permissions.name: View System Log
permissions.text: without it, the sync fails with an error instead of skipping log events.

steps.title: Sign in as a Read-only Administrator
steps.text: Sign in to the Okta admin console as a Read-only Administrator, so the token gets that role. Use a long-lived admin account.

steps.title: Create a token
steps.text: Open Security, API, Tokens and create a token. Set where API calls made with this token must come from: Any IP, unless you have a network zone for HydraDB's addresses. Without this setting, creating the token fails with an unclear error.

steps.title: Check the role
steps.text: In the token list, check the Role column to confirm the role the token got.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the token as `api_key` and your org's API address as `service_url`, with `/api/v1/` and the trailing slash.

steps.title: Nothing to select
steps.text: Okta has no resources to choose. The connector reads the whole org.

connect.account: One connector reads one Okta org.

sync.first_sync: Users, groups, applications, group members, application assignments and MFA factors are read in full. System Log events reach back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads the whole directory again, and System Log events newer than the last sync. Users, groups and applications that did not change are skipped.
sync.edits: A change to a user, group or application updates its document. A change only to a group's members, an application's assignments or a user's MFA factors may not show until the group, application or user itself changes.
sync.deletes: Users, groups and applications deleted in Okta can stay searchable in HydraDB. A removed MFA factor can stay listed on the user.
notes: MFA factors are read one user at a time, with a one-second pause per user. If one user's factors cannot be read, that user's factors are skipped and the sync goes on. If Okta rejects the token, the sync fails.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

documents.name: Users
documents.title: The first and last name, else the login, else `Okta user` with the user's id.
documents.text: The name, then `Login`, `Email`, `Title`, `Department`, `Manager`, `Organization`, `Location`, `Second Email`, `Mobile Phone`, `Status`, `MFA`, `Created` and `Last Login` lines. Profile attributes outside this list are not synced. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the user was last updated in Okta, else when it was created.

attributes.name: email
attributes.text: The primary email, written as the `Email` line. Identifies the user as a person in the graph. The name does not.

attributes.name: first_name, last_name
attributes.text: The user's name, used for the title and the first line.

attributes.name: login
attributes.text: The username, written as the `Login` line. It is the title when the user has no name.

attributes.name: job_title, department, organization
attributes.text: Written as the `Title`, `Department` and `Organization` lines.

attributes.name: manager
attributes.text: The manager's name from the profile, written as the `Manager` line. It does not create the manager link.

attributes.name: managerId
attributes.text: Links the user to their manager's user record when it matches exactly one user by id, employee number or login, ignoring case. Not kept as a field. Not searchable.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: The account state, written as the `Status` line.

attributes.name: mfa_factors
attributes.text: The active factor types and providers HydraDB found, written as the `MFA` line. A missing factor does not prove MFA is off: a user's factor read can fail and be skipped, and a removed factor can stay listed.

attributes.name: created
attributes.text: When the user was created, written as the `Created` line. The result date when the user has no last-updated time.

attributes.name: last_login
attributes.text: The last recorded login, written as the `Last Login` line. Not used as the result date.

attributes.name: last_updated
attributes.text: When the user was last updated in Okta. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.okta_user_id
attributes.text: The Okta user id. Picks out one user. Not searchable.

attributes.name: activated
attributes.text: When the account was activated.

documents.name: Groups
documents.one_document: One Okta group, with its members.
documents.title: The group name, else `Okta group` with the group's id.
documents.text: The name, then `Description`, `Type`, `Members` and `Created` lines. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the group was last updated in Okta, else when it was created.

attributes.name: description
attributes.text: The group description.

attributes.name: group_type
attributes.text: Whether the group is managed in Okta, comes from an application, or is built in.

attributes.name: members
attributes.text: Up to 200 distinct member names, with a count of the rest and of members without a name. Each member is linked to their user record.

attributes.name: Source application
attributes.text: A group that comes from an application is linked to that application's record. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created
attributes.text: When the group was created, written as the `Created` line. The result date when the group has no last-updated time.

attributes.name: last_updated
attributes.text: When the group was last updated in Okta. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.okta_group_id
attributes.text: The Okta group id. Picks out one group. Not searchable.

attributes.name: member_count
attributes.text: How many members the group has, including any beyond the 200 names in the text.

documents.name: Applications
documents.one_document: One Okta application, with its assignments.
documents.title: The application label, else its internal name, else `Okta application` with its id.
documents.text: The label, then `App`, `Status`, `Sign-On Mode`, `Assigned Users` and `Created` lines. Assigned groups are not written into the text. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the application was last updated in Okta, else when it was created.

attributes.name: name
attributes.text: The internal app name, written as the `App` line. It is the title when the application has no label.

attributes.name: status, sign_on_mode
attributes.text: The application state and its sign-on mode, such as `SAML_2_0`.

attributes.name: assigned_users
attributes.text: Up to 200 distinct assigned user names, with a count of the rest. Each assigned user is linked to the application.

attributes.name: Assigned groups
attributes.text: Each group assigned to the application is linked to it. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created
attributes.text: When the application was created, written as the `Created` line. The result date when the application has no last-updated time.

attributes.name: last_updated
attributes.text: When the application was last updated in Okta. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.okta_application_id
attributes.text: The Okta application id. Picks out one application. Not searchable.

attributes.name: assigned_user_count, assigned_group_count
attributes.text: How many users and groups are assigned to the application.

documents.name: System Log events
documents.title: The event's display message, else its event type, else `Okta event` with its id.
documents.text: The message, then `Event Type`, `Outcome`, `Actor`, `Severity` and `Published` lines. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.text: The event type, written as the `Event Type` line. It is the title when the event has no display message.

attributes.name: outcome, severity
attributes.text: The result with its reason, and the severity.

attributes.name: actor
attributes.text: Who performed the action, by display name, else alternate id, else id, written as the `Actor` line. The event is linked to that person's user record.

attributes.name: Targets
attributes.text: The users, applications and groups the event acted on. The event is linked to each of their records. Not searchable.

attributes.name: published
attributes.text: When the event happened, written as the `Published` line.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.okta_log_uuid
attributes.text: The event's Okta id. Picks out one event. Not searchable.

example_searches: Which members are listed for the Engineering-Admins group?
Which recorded sign-in events failed yesterday?
Who is linked as this user's manager?

connections: A group to each of its members.
A group that comes from an application to that application.
An application to each assigned user and group.
A System Log event to the user who performed it, and to each user, application or group it acted on.
A link is made only when its target was synced by this connector. Each item has at most 200 links.
No links to items in other tools.
people: Each user, identified by primary email.
Groups and applications are linked records, not people.
Managers, members, assignees and event actors are linked to user records, not added as separate people.
graph.from_text: The text of users, groups, applications and events, including department, organization and location.

not_synced: Policies, authorization servers, network zones and admin role assignments.
Custom profile attributes outside the fields listed above.
System Log events older than the sync window.
Member and assignee names beyond 200 per group or application, and links beyond 200 per item.
Group memberships and application assignments as their own documents. They are shown on the group or application.
Deletions: users, groups, applications and MFA factors deleted in Okta can stay in HydraDB.
